source: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training & Conditioning / Squat University
biomechanical_root_cause: Limited ankle dorsiflexion mobility preventing the knee from tracking over the toes, or tight adductor magnus and hip capsule restricting depth. Often exacerbated by a stance width that is too narrow for the lifter's hip socket anatomy.
verbal_cues: Spread the floor apart with your feet to create space for your hips to sink.
Sit between your ankles, not back behind your heels.
Open your knees out in the direction of your toes as you descend.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell at chest level. Pause at the bottom target height to build hip mobility and positional comfort in the hole.
Anchor a heavy resistance band low behind you and loop it across the talus bone of the front ankle. Lunge forward to drive knee over toe.

source: Starting Strength (Mark Rippetoe) / Juggernaut Training Systems
biomechanical_root_cause: Quadriceps fatigue or relative weakness causes the lifter to shift the load backward onto the stronger posterior chain (hamstrings, glutes, spinal erectors). Can also stem from a collapsing thoracic spine and lack of lat engagement under the barbell.
verbal_cues: Show the logo on your chest to the wall in front of you.
Drive your traps and upper back aggressively up into the bar out of the hole.
Keep your ribs pulled down and brace your core 360 degrees before descending.

corrective_drills.drill: Front Squats or Safety Squat Bar (SSB) Squats
corrective_drills.coaching_points: Forces an upright vertical torso; any excessive forward lean results in dropping the bar, immediately reinforcing upright posture and quad recruitment.

corrective_drills.drill: Thoracic Extension over Foam Roller + Lat Pullovers
corrective_drills.coaching_points: Mobilizes the thoracic spine to prevent mid-back rounding under heavy axial loads.

biomechanical_root_cause: Relying on the passive stretch reflex and bounce at the bottom rather than active eccentric muscular tension. Increases shear stress across the patellar tendon and ACL.
verbal_cues: Pull yourself down with your hip flexors under control; do not just fall.
Count two seconds on the way down: 'One-one-thousand, Two-one-thousand'.
Stay tight like a compressed spring at the bottom.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: 3 seconds eccentric descent, 1 second pause in the hole, 1 second explosive ascent. Re-establishes neuromuscular motor control.

biomechanical_root_cause: Prematurely initiating the subsequent rep before achieving full knee and hip extension, or glute amnesia where the lifter fails to squeeze glutes at the top.
verbal_cues: Stand tall and proud at the top of every rep.
Squeeze your glutes and lock your knees before starting the next rep.

corrective_drills.drill: Standing Glute Bridges / Banded Hip Extensions
corrective_drills.coaching_points: Focus on terminal hip extension without hyperextending the lumbar spine.
